name: Kurt Wagner

summary: Kurt's birth was planned by the mutant couple Mystique and Destiny. Destiny, a clairvoyant, foresaw that the demonic mutant Azazel would one day escape his prison dimension and seize the world, so she set out to raise a good-hearted child of his blood who could stand against him. Mystique married a Bavarian nobleman, Baron Christian Wagner, as cover, began an affair with Azazel, then copied his genetic template with her shapeshifting to make Destiny pregnant. When the Baron discovered the two women and tried to have them killed, Mystique murdered him. The baby was born with Azazel's demonic features and Mystique's blue colouring, and once a local mob turned on the household, Destiny slipped away with him. In older tellings Mystique is simply his birth mother, who abandoned the child she had with Azazel.

The infant was found floating down a river by the sorceress Margali Szardos, who raised him alongside her own children, Stefan and Jimaine, inside a travelling German circus called Der Jahrmarkt. Billed as a blue devil, Kurt endured cruelty from the circus owner but found comfort in his Catholic faith and became a star trapeze artist, with audiences assuming his looks were a costume. He fell for Jimaine, and his teleportation first surfaced when he jumped to catch her during a fall. He and Stefan swore a blood oath that Kurt would stop him if he ever killed without cause.

When the circus was sold and he faced being shown as a freak, Kurt ran away, survived an attempt to shoot him by teleporting in a cloud of sulphur, and was taken in by a village priest, Father Wagner, whose surname he later adopted. Around then Stefan went mad and murdered children near Winzeldorf; Kurt tracked him down and killed him by accident in the struggle. The villagers took Kurt for a demon and were about to lynch him when Professor Charles Xavier stopped the mob with his mind and invited him to join the X-Men. Under the codename Nightcrawler he went with Cyclops and the other new recruits to rescue the original team from the living island Krakoa, and stayed on afterwards.

comics.title: The gentle teleporter
comics.summary: After the Krakoa mission Kurt stays with Xavier's new team and quickly becomes its warmest member, befriending the prickly Wolverine as well as Storm and Colossus. He learns he can all but vanish in shadow, starts dating the flight attendant Amanda Sefton and, on his birthday, has his soul stolen by Margali Szardos, who blames him for Stefan's death until Doctor Strange shows her the truth and Amanda is revealed to be Jimaine. Locked in a featureless cell during a clash with Arcade and Doctor Doom, he risks a blind teleport and ends up high in the sky above Doom's castle before diving to safety in a lake.

comics.title: From God Loves, Man Kills to the Mutant Massacre
comics.summary: The preacher William Stryker holds Kurt up as proof that mutants are demonic, while the X-Men fight his Purifiers. In his first solo series an accident in the Danger Room throws him through a string of fairy-tale worlds of sky pirates, sorcerers and his own cartoon look-alikes, the Bamfs. For a time he leads the X-Men in the field, then recovers his spirit by foiling Arcade's plot against a lost queen. During the Marauders' slaughter of the Morlocks he is badly hurt by Riptide and slips into a coma.

comics.title: Founding Excalibur
comics.summary: Waking on Muir Island to news that the X-Men have died, Kurt and Kitty Pryde team up with Captain Britain, Meggan and Rachel Summers to fight off the bounty hunters of Technet, and the group forms Excalibur in the X-Men's memory, based in Brian Braddock's lighthouse. Kurt naturally becomes field leader, leads the team on a long trip across alternate worlds and ends up with a broken leg when Brian's jealousy over Meggan boils over. The run's first stretch ends with the team defeating Necrom and freeing itself from the schemes of Merlyn and Roma.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Excalibur Special Edition Vol 1 #1

comics.title: Mystique's son
comics.summary: Graydon Creed reveals that he and Kurt are half-brothers, both sons of Mystique, and when Kurt confronts her he learns she deliberately left him to die as a baby; Rogue becomes the closest thing he has to a sister. Soon afterwards he battles the fear demon D'Spayre to save Margali and forgives her for hiding his past, accepting her as his mother. Leading Excalibur through a demonic attack on London and the loss of Amanda to Limbo, he finally returns to America with Kitty and Colossus after Meggan and Brian's wedding, and the team breaks up.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: X-Men Unlimited Vol 1 #4

comics.title: Father Wagner and the Holy War
comics.summary: Kurt enters the Catholic Church as a postulant and starts celebrating Mass at St. Michael's while still serving with the X-Men, surviving an assassination attempt by a faction of Neo who blame the team for their losses. His studies are steered by a mentor whose guidance leaves him more confused, and he steps down as team leader. Eventually he learns that the anti-mutant Church of Humanity staged his mentorship and even his ordination, planning to raise him toward the papacy and then expose him as a mutant; he renounces the priesthood and the X-Men bring the cult down.

comics.title: Son of Azazel
comics.summary: Kurt's will is taken over and he joins dozens of other mutant teleporters on a Bermuda Triangle island to open a gateway for Azazel's army. Freed in Azazel's realm, he learns that he is one of Azazel's children and that Margali had a hand in the plan. Azazel offers him a place at his side; Kurt refuses, beats his father in a duel and escapes home, determined not to be defined by where he came from.

comics.title: The last jump
comics.summary: On Utopia Kurt worries that the X-Men are losing their way, and he objects openly when his teammates use lethal force to protect the returning Hope. With Bastion targeting every mutant teleporter and Magik trapped in Limbo, he is left to carry Hope across the country in a chain of jumps. In Las Vegas, exhausted, he puts himself between Hope and Bastion, takes a fatal blow and, praying for strength, makes one last teleport that lands her safely on Utopia before he dies. His funeral leaves Wolverine shattered and Beast blaming Cyclops.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Uncanny X-Men Vol 1 #524

comics.title: The Quest for Nightcrawler
comics.summary: In the afterlife Kurt leads a fight against Azazel's demonic pirates, recruiting some of Azazel's Bamfs by promising them his soul; on Earth the creatures overrun the Jean Grey School. When the X-Men are pulled into the struggle he captains a stolen ship to rescue them, and after Azazel wounds Wolverine he gives up his place in paradise, taking a new body made from Bamfs to stop his father on Earth. Back at the school he reconnects with Amanda Sefton, only to lose her again when she seals herself in the realm he left behind.

comics.title: Way of X and Legion of X
comics.summary: Kurt dies on the raid that destroys Orchis' Mother Mold, is resurrected on Krakoa and joins its ruling Quiet Council. Uneasy with a culture where death has become routine, he searches for a new spiritual path for mutants, works with Legion against the psychic parasite Onslaught and founds the Spark and the Legionaries, a peacekeeping force with himself as Krakoa's chief lawman. Orchis later corrupts him through Margali Szardos and forces him to murder three anti-mutant heads of state; freed and resurrected, he leaves Krakoa under the shadow of those killings.

comics.title: Uncanny Spider-Man and the fall of Krakoa
comics.summary: To make amends, Kurt puts on a spare Spider-Man suit, takes up the Hopesword and patrols New York as a street-level hero he calls Spinnenmann, though locals nickname him Hellcrawler. As one of the few mutants left active after Orchis attacks Krakoa, he dodges Sentinels and Orchis hunters, falls for the mercenary Silver Sable and finally talks openly with Mystique about his parentage. He then rejoins the X-Men for the final push against Orchis, raiding its space station alongside Wolverine and Colossus.

screen.title: X2
screen.summary: This Kurt is a devout German circus performer whose blue skin is covered in self-made marks of faith. Brainwashed by William Stryker, he opens the film by teleporting through the White House and nearly assassinating the President, then is tracked down by Storm and Jean. He helps Storm rescue the kidnapped students at Alkali Lake and stop Stryker's Cerebro, and stands with the X-Men when Xavier briefs the President at the end.

screen.title: X-Men: Apocalypse
screen.summary: In 1983 Kurt is forced into an East Berlin cage fight against Angel until Mystique frees him and brings him to Xavier's school. After the mansion is destroyed he teleports himself, Scott and Jean onto Stryker's helicopter, helps free the captured adults at Alkali Lake and, in Cairo, rescues Xavier from En Sabah Nur. He ends the film as a member of the new X-Men.

screen.title: Deadpool 2
screen.summary: Nightcrawler is among the X-Men briefly seen in a room at Xavier's school while Colossus chats with Deadpool in the corridor. As Deadpool asks where everyone else is, Beast gently closes the door to keep them out of sight.

screen.title: Dark Phoenix
screen.summary: Kurt is part of the X-Men when a mission in space leaves Jean Grey carrying an unstable cosmic power. As she loses control the team fractures, and it has to reunite against D'Bari aliens who want the force for themselves. The wiki's synopsis is brief and does not describe Kurt's individual role.

trivia.fact: Dave Cockrum first sketched the character while serving in the US Navy on Guam, during a typhoon that kept him awake, and offered him to DC's Legion of Super-Heroes before coming to Marvel; DC turned the design down.

Teleporting upward fights both gravity and Earth's magnetic field, which makes it the hardest jump he can make. His record is a blind vertical leap of about a mile out of a sealed cell in Doctor Doom's castle.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Uncanny X-Men Vol 1 #147 (July 1981)

trivia.fact: When Kurt became a Spider-Man in 2023, the names tossed around for him included Antispider, Darkweb, Shadowspider and Terrorspinner. He settled on Spinnenmann, German for Spider-Man, while New Yorkers called him Hellcrawler.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Uncanny Spider-Man Vol 1 #1 (November 2023)

trivia.fact: Writer Chris Claremont toyed early on with making Mystique Kurt's father and Destiny his mother, an idea dropped at the time. A version of it became canon decades later in X-Men Blue: Origins #1, where Mystique uses Azazel's genetic template to father Kurt with Destiny.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: X-Men Blue: Origins Vol 1 #1 (January 2024)

unverified: Avengers: Doomsday (unreleased) appears in the MCU Wiki infobox for Nightcrawler with Alan Cumming credited. It is left out and no plot details were researched.
Avengers: Endgame Encore re-release (25 September 2026): the MCU Wiki's Encore plot summary and Encore-exclusive cast list do not include Nightcrawler in any version, so no entry was added.

Deadpool 2 (2018): the Marvel Fandom wiki tags Nightcrawler as a cameo but does not name the performer on the film page or the character page, so the actor field says so. The film page notes the X-Men cameo was directed by Simon Kinberg on the Dark Phoenix set and added by green screen.
Deadpool & Wolverine (2024): neither the MCU Wiki film page nor the Marvel Fandom film page lists Nightcrawler at all, so there is no entry.

X-Men: The Last Stand (2006): Kurt does not appear. The Marvel Fandom wiki says Alan Cumming did not return; his absence is explained in X-Men: The Official Game, a video game, which does not count as a screen appearance.
Dark Phoenix (2019): the Marvel Fandom plot section is a short trailer-style blurb and Kurt's Earth-10005 page stops after Apocalypse, so the summary sticks to the film's premise.
Not counted: X-Men '97 and other animation, X-Men: The Official Game, and the X-Men 2 Prequel: Nightcrawler comic, which the wiki uses for his film-universe backstory.
Both Fox character pages note that the films leave any family link between Kurt and Mystique ambiguous.

Parentage has been retold several times. The origin follows the current account (X-Men Blue: Origins #1, January 2024) and notes the older version in which Mystique is his birth mother (X-Men Unlimited #4, Uncanny X-Men #429).
Issue numbering: the character page cites Uncanny X-Men #210 for Riptide's attack, but the #211 issue page (November 1986) is the one that describes it, so the era uses #211.
The Cockrum design story rests on the wiki's citation of a 1993 Wizard special, which is not an allowed source and was not checked.

Several issue pages have no plot synopsis (Excalibur #50 and #125, X-Men Unlimited #4, X-Men Vol 2 #101, Uncanny X-Men #423, Amazing X-Men Vol 2 #5, Nightcrawler Vol 4 #1, Way of X #1, Legion of X #1, Sons of X #1, Uncanny Spider-Man #1 and #5, X-Men Blue: Origins #1, Fall of the House of X #3), and the Draco issues have only one-line summaries. Those details rest on the Earth-616 character page.
The character page's latest entry (X-Men Vol 6 #35, August 2024), a brief reunion with Rogue, Mystique and Destiny, is not given its own era.
Deadpool 2: actor note was "Uncredited cameo; the performer is not named on the wiki"
